Title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in get_swagger_ui_html due to unsanitized parameters
Analysis:
### Source:
`openapi_url`, `oauth2_redirect_url`, and `title` arguments passed into `get_swagger_ui_html()`. In standard deployments, the `openapi_url` and `oauth2_redirect_url` are concatenated with `root_path` which is extracted directly from the request scope (`req.scope.get("root_path", "")`). A malicious client can supply a crafted `root_path` via HTTP headers (such as `X-Forwarded-Prefix`, depending on the proxy setup).

### Sanitization/Validation:
None. The parameters are directly formatted using f-string interpolation into the HTML output without any escaping, sanitization, or validation.

### Sink:
The f-string interpolated HTML string is returned in an `HTMLResponse`, which is then executed by the browser. Because `openapi_url` and `oauth2_redirect_url` are formatted within single quotes inside a `<script>` tag, supplying a payload with a single quote (`'`) allows escaping the JS string literal and executing arbitrary JavaScript.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
1. For dynamic parameters:
If a developer dynamically passes a user-controlled parameter (e.g., query string or dynamic configuration) to `title` or `openapi_url`:
```python
@app.get("/custom-docs")
async def get_docs(title: str):
    return get_swagger_ui_html(openapi_url="/openapi.json", title=title)
```
Request: `GET /custom-docs?title=%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C/script%3E`

2. For proxy header / `root_path` injection:
If the application proxy translates `X-Forwarded-Prefix` to `root_path` in `scope["root_path"]`:
Request:
```http
GET /docs HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8000
X-Forwarded-Prefix: '; alert(1); //
```
This causes the generated HTML's script block to render:
```javascript
const ui = SwaggerUIBundle({
    url: ''; alert(1); ///openapi.json',
```
This executes `alert(1)` immediately on page load.
Snippet:
def get_swagger_ui_html( *, openapi_url: Annotated[ str, Doc( """ The OpenAPI URL that Swagger UI should load and use. This is normally done automatically by FastAPI using the default URL `/openapi.json`. """ ), ], title: Annotated[ str, Doc( """ The HTML `` content, normally shown in the browser tab. """ ), ], swagger_js_url: Annotated[ str, Doc( """ The URL to use to load the Swagger UI JavaScript. It is normally set to a CDN URL. """ ), ] = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/swagger-ui-dist@5.9.0/swagger-ui-bundle.js", swagger_css_url: Annotated[ str, Doc( """ The URL to use to load the Swagger UI CSS. It is normally set to a CDN URL. """ ), ] = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/swagger-ui-dist@5.9.0/swagger-ui.css", swagger_favicon_url: Annotated[ str, Doc( """ The URL of the favicon to use. It is normally shown in the browser tab. """ ), ] = "https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/img/favicon.png", oauth2_redirect_url: Annotated[ Optional[str], Doc( """ The OAuth2 redirect URL, it is normally automatically handled by FastAPI. Title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in get_redoc_html due to unsanitized parameters
Analysis:
### Source:
`openapi_url`, `title`, `redoc_favicon_url` or `redoc_js_url` arguments passed into `get_redoc_html()`. In standard deployments, the `openapi_url` is concatenated with `root_path` which is extracted directly from the request scope (`req.scope.get("root_path", "")`). A malicious client can supply a crafted `root_path` via HTTP headers (such as `X-Forwarded-Prefix`, depending on the proxy setup).

### Sanitization/Validation:
None. The parameters are directly formatted using f-string interpolation into the HTML output without any escaping, sanitization, or validation.

### Sink:
The f-string interpolated HTML string is returned in an `HTMLResponse`, which is then executed by the browser. Because `openapi_url` is formatted within a raw HTML tag `<redoc spec-url="{openapi_url}"></redoc>`, supplying a payload with a double quote (`"`) allows escaping the tag attribute and injecting arbitrary script tags or executing arbitrary HTML/JavaScript.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
1. For dynamic parameters:
If a developer dynamically passes a user-controlled parameter (e.g., query string or dynamic configuration) to `title` or `openapi_url`:
```python
@app.get("/custom-redoc")
async def get_redoc(title: str):
    return get_redoc_html(openapi_url="/openapi.json", title=title)
```
Request: `GET /custom-redoc?title=%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C/script%3E`

2. For proxy header / `root_path` injection:
If the application proxy translates `X-Forwarded-Prefix` to `root_path` in `scope["root_path"]`:
Request:
```http
GET /redoc HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8000
X-Forwarded-Prefix: "><script>alert(1)</script>
```
This causes the generated HTML to render:
```html
<redoc spec-url=""><script>alert(1)</script>/openapi.json"></redoc>
```
This executes `alert(1)` immediately on page load.
Snippet:
def get_redoc_html(
    *,
    openapi_url: Annotated[
        str,
        Doc(
            """
            The OpenAPI URL that ReDoc should load and use.

            This is normally done automatically by FastAPI using the default URL
            `/openapi.json`.
            """
        ),
    ],
    title: Annotated[
        str,
        Doc(
            """
            The HTML `<title>` content, normally shown in the browser tab.
            """
        ),
    ],
    redoc_js_url: Annotated[
        str,
        Doc(
            """
            The URL to use to load the ReDoc JavaScript.

            It is normally set to a CDN URL.
            """
        ),
    ] = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/redoc@next/bundles/redoc.standalone.js",
    redoc_favicon_url: Annotated[
        str,
        Doc(
            """
            The URL of the favicon to use. It is normally shown in the browser tab.
            """
        ),
    ] = "https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/img/favicon.png",
    with_google_fonts: Annotated[
        bool,
        Doc(
            """
            Load and use Google Fonts.
            """
        ),
    ] = True,
) -> HTMLResponse:
    html = f"""
    <!DOCTYPE html>
    <html>
    <head>
    <title>{title}</title>
    <!-- needed for adaptive design -->
    <meta charset="utf-8"/>
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    """
    if with_google_fonts:
        html += """
    <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Montserrat:300,400,700|Roboto:300,400,700" rel="stylesheet">
    """
    html += f"""
    <link rel="shortcut icon" href="{redoc_favicon_url}">
    <!--
    ReDoc doesn't change outer page styles
    -->
    <style>
      body {{
        margin: 0;
        padding: 0;
      }}
    </style>
    </head>
    <body>
    <noscript>
        ReDoc requires Javascript to function. Please enable it to browse the documentation.
    </noscript>
    <redoc spec-url="{openapi_url}"></redoc>
    <script src="{redoc_js_url}"> </script>
    </body>
    </html>
    """
    return HTMLResponse(html)

Title: Open Redirect in OAuth2 Filter via Unvalidated State Parameter
Analysis:
An Open Redirect vulnerability (CWE-601) exists in Envoy's OAuth2 HTTP Filter (`OAuth2Filter`).

When a user initiates the OAuth login flow, `OAuth2Filter::redirectToOAuthServer` constructs the authorization endpoint redirect URL, passing a user-controlled callback state path in the `state` query parameter. This parameter represents the URL where the browser should be redirected after successful authentication.

Upon receiving the authentication callback at `/_oauth`, `OAuth2Filter::decodeHeaders` extracts the `state` parameter from the query string (lines 403-414). The filter parses the parameter using `Http::Utility::Url::initialize` (lines 416-417), but does not perform any validation to ensure that the parsed URL is restricted to the local domain/host or matches a configured safe whitelist.

After successful token acquisition, `OAuth2Filter::finishGetAccessTokenFlow` constructs a `302 Found` redirect response and sets the `Location` header to the unvalidated `state_` URL (line 619), leading to an open redirect.

Additionally, a similar issue occurs during a redirect race condition at lines 349-353, where the unvalidated decoded query parameter `state` is used directly in a redirect.

An attacker can exploit this by crafting a malicious authentication link with a modified `state` parameter pointing to an external domain (e.g., `https://malicious.com`). Once a victim authenticates successfully, Envoy redirects them to the attacker-controlled site, facilitating credential harvesting or phishing attacks.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
1. Attacker sends a victim a link to log in:
   GET /_oauth?code=AUTHORIZATION_CODE&state=https%3A%2F%2Fevil-attacker.com%2Fphish HTTP/1.1
   Host: secure-envoy-gateway.com

2. Envoy processes the callback, fetches the access token, and calls finishGetAccessTokenFlow().
3. Envoy issues a redirect to the attacker's site:
   HTTP/1.1 302 Found
   Location: https://evil-attacker.com/phish
   Set-Cookie: OauthHMAC=...

Title: Open Redirect in OAuth2 Filter Race Condition Mitigation
Analysis:
An Open Redirect vulnerability (CWE-601) exists in Envoy's OAuth2 HTTP Filter (`OAuth2Filter`) under race conditions during successful logins.

If multiple requests are initiated concurrently, some may result in a race condition on the callback path. `OAuth2Filter::decodeHeaders` catches this scenario when the requested path matches the configured redirect path (lines 319-328). It parses the user-supplied `state` query parameter and decodes it (lines 330-335).

It initializes a URL object with the decoded state parameter (lines 336-341), but fails to validate that the host or domain of `state` is restricted to local/trusted domains. It then constructs a `302 Found` response redirecting directly to the unvalidated `state` URL (lines 349-354).

An attacker can exploit this callback race condition behavior to perform open redirects (e.g., redirecting to `https://evil-attacker.com/`).

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
GET /_oauth?state=https%3A%2F%2Fevil-attacker.com%2F HTTP/1.1
Host: secure-envoy-gateway.com
Cookie: [Valid cookies to satisfy canSkipOAuth]

Response:
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: https://evil-attacker.com/
